title: Kent County Council: Using predictive analytics to prevent homelessness in Maidstone and Kent
summary: Kent County Council reports that under 1% of households flagged by a Xantura predictive-analytics platform and given proactive support became homeless, against 40% of an unsupported group.
account: Maidstone Borough Council uses an AI-enabled Xantura platform to flag households for proactive homelessness support. On 10 January 2024 Nesta reported that a Maidstone Borough Council officer had told a Nesta panel that only 2% of the first flagged cohort became homeless after early intervention. In a presentation published on 4 November 2024, Kent describes Maidstone’s use of the platform and a wider county pilot. The council presenter reports that fewer than 1% of supported alerted households became homeless, compared with 40% of a group that lacked support because of limited capacity. The comparison was not randomized and does not separate AI’s effect from the support intervention. The presenter does not date these outcomes. In December 2025 the government's National Plan to End Homelessness reported that from June 2023 to January 2025 the approach saved £440,000 in temporary accommodation and avoided 96 homelessness cases. The government does not state how these figures were calculated. A randomized trial of similar data-led outreach with Xantura in four other councils was still in progress in June 2026.
purpose: Identify households at risk of homelessness so that councils can offer proactive support.
system: Xantura AI-enabled predictive-analytics platform used for homelessness prevention
deployer: Maidstone Borough Council and Kent County Council with participating district and borough councils

ratings.reason: The council reports that proactive support prevented homelessness in a high-risk cohort. The groups were not randomized, and AI’s separate effect is unknown.

The government reports that the approach increased prevention effectiveness by 65% and avoided 96 homelessness cases from June 2023 to January 2025. No source supplies sample sizes or an independent evaluation.

ai_role.statement: The presenter describes an AI-enabled platform that combines council data and flags households for human support. The prevention comparison concerns the combined targeting-and-support program. Because support was capacity-constrained and not randomized, AI’s separate contribution to the difference is not established.

brief: Maidstone Borough Council uses an AI-enabled Xantura platform to flag households for proactive homelessness support. In a presentation published on 4 November 2024, a Kent County Council presenter reports that fewer than 1% of flagged households that received support became homeless, against 40% of a group that went without support because the housing team lacked capacity. The groups were not randomized, and the comparison does not separate the effect of the targeting from that of the support. The presenter does not date these outcomes.[1] The UK government's National Plan to End Homelessness, published on 11 December 2025, features Maidstone's use of the platform. Its figures for June 2023 to January 2025 include £440,000 saved in temporary accommodation and 96 homelessness cases avoided, with no stated method.[2] The Centre for Homelessness Impact's randomized trial of similar data-led outreach with Xantura in four other councils was still in progress in June 2026. A family screening tool in a Pennsylvania county also scores households from administrative data, and its scores allegedly fell unevenly on Black families. Kent's presenter states that protected characteristics are not included in the live prediction model.

fields.headline: Kent reports fewer homeless households after targeted support

value.role: SHA-256 of the complete public record and its assessments

provenance.basis: SHA-256 of the public record, its assessments, and its displayed answers and notes, excluding its own identifier and the derived coverage summary.

fields.account: Maidstone Borough Council uses an AI-enabled Xantura platform to flag households for proactive homelessness support. On 10 January 2024 Nesta reported that a Maidstone Borough Council officer had told a Nesta panel that only 2% of the first flagged cohort became homeless after early intervention. In a presentation published on 4 November 2024, Kent describes Maidstone’s use of the platform and a wider county pilot. The council presenter reports that fewer than 1% of supported alerted households became homeless, compared with 40% of a group that lacked support because of limited capacity. The comparison was not randomized and does not separate AI’s effect from the support intervention. The presenter does not date these outcomes. In December 2025 the government's National Plan to End Homelessness reported that from June 2023 to January 2025 the approach saved £440,000 in temporary accommodation and avoided 96 homelessness cases. The government does not state how these figures were calculated. A randomized trial of similar data-led outreach with Xantura in four other councils was still in progress in June 2026.

produced_by: Maidstone combined local data with data shared by Kent County Council, including social-care information.
The comparison group did not receive proactive support because the housing team lacked capacity.
must_hold: The presenter states that protected characteristics are not included in the live prediction model.
The source does not establish causal conditions for reproducing the prevention result.

echoes.setting: Maidstone Borough Council's earlier OneView homelessness prevention work with EY and Xantura, which won a Local Government Chronicle award.
Centre for Homelessness Impact randomized trial of data-led outreach with Xantura in Barking and Dagenham, Stockport, Test Valley and Newham, evaluated by Verian Group and Simetrica-Jacobs.
